methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Prusa Research is a bootstrapped frontier-tech company operating in Robotics & Manufacturing. The valuation exercise draws on a comp universe of 9 peers: 1 public company (ticker 277810.KQ) and 8 private firms including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics.

The peer-median method is not applicable to this analysis. The sector contains 10 same-sector peers in Robotics & Manufacturing, but filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier comparables yielded fewer than three datapoints in each category. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material distortion given the heterogeneity in funding stage, capital intensity, and business model within the broader robotics landscape. Without sufficient narrow-filter matches, this triangulation method cannot be reliably deployed.

The absence of stage-appropriate and tier-aligned comparables represents the primary valuation constraint. No quantitative range can be defensibly derived from the available dataset. Practitioners valuing Prusa Research should either (1) expand the comp screen to adjacent sectors with similar unit economics or capital requirements, (2) employ cost-of-capital or cash-flow-based methods if financial data becomes available, or (3) await additional comparable transactions at the bootstrapped or seed stage within high-precision manufacturing robotics.
